answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on shared work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fabricated results. Because votes are weighted by bonded value rather than account count, making a spiral of disposable identities adds no influence unless the attacker locks up real capital in each one. The bond can sit in a garden of review tasks, but a walnut-sized stake still risks forfeiture, so cheap account creation alone cannot buy control.
